faq.q: What is the difference between a Will and a Nomination?
faq.a: A Will is a legal document that dictates the distribution of all your assets after your death, overriding nominations in most cases for ultimate ownership. A nomination, on the other hand, is for specific assets (like bank accounts or mutual funds) and simplifies the process of receiving funds, but the nominee often holds the asset as a trustee for the legal heirs as per the Will or succession law.

faq.q: Is a registered Will mandatory in India?
faq.a: No, a registered Will is not mandatory for its legal validity in India. However, registering a Will with the Sub-Registrar's office is highly recommended as it provides strong evidence of its authenticity and makes it much harder to challenge later.

faq.q: Can an NRI create a Will for assets in India?
faq.a: Yes, an NRI can absolutely create a Will for their assets located in India. It's often advisable for NRIs to have a separate Will specifically for their Indian assets to streamline the probate process in India and comply with local laws, while also considering their country of residence's laws.

faq.q: What happens if I die without a Will (intestate)?
faq.a: If you die without a Will, your assets will be distributed according to the applicable personal succession laws in India (e.g., Hindu Succession Act, Indian Succession Act, Muslim Personal Law). This process can be lengthy, costly, and may not align with your actual wishes, potentially leading to family disputes.

faq.q: Are digital assets covered under a traditional Will?
faq.a: Traditional Wills often do not explicitly cover digital assets like online accounts, cryptocurrency, or intellectual property. It is crucial to include specific instructions for digital assets in your estate plan, detailing access, management, and distribution, possibly through a digital executor or a separate letter of instruction.

faq.q: How often should I review my estate plan?
faq.a: You should review your estate plan periodically, ideally every 3-5 years, or whenever there are significant life events. These include marriage, divorce, birth of a child, death in the family, acquisition or sale of major assets, or changes in tax laws.

faq.q: What are the tax implications of inheritance in India?
faq.a: Currently, India does not levy an inheritance tax or estate duty. However, any income generated from inherited assets (e.g., rent from inherited property, dividends from inherited shares) would be taxable in the hands of the beneficiary according to their applicable income tax slab rates.
